title: Bounded parsing and length check
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean finite Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For every pair of Boolean words $\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{rest}$ with $x=\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{rest}$ and every natural number $r\le |c.output|$, the machine obtained by augmenting $M$ with the pair parser, started on the first symbol of $\mathrm{rest}$ with the extra tape containing $\mathrm{pre}\,c.output$ and positioned at cell $r-1$, halts within at most $|\mathrm{rest}|+1$ steps and outputs the single bit that is $1$ exactly when the pair parser decodes $\mathrm{rest}$ as $(a,b)$ for some $a,b$ with $|b|\le r$, and is $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a Boolean finite Turing machine
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
caveat: The auxiliary machine and its starting configuration are specified by private constructions in the formal snippet; the prose describes their relevant setup and behavior.
